sources.title: Unskilled and unaware of it: How difficulties in recognizing one's own incompetence lead to inflated self-assessments
sources.publisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 77(6), 1121-1134

sources.title: The Dunning-Kruger effect is (mostly) a statistical artefact: Valid approaches to testing the hypothesis with individual differences data

concepts.definition: The finding that low performers overestimate and high performers slightly underestimate their performance.
The statistical tendency of extreme values to be followed by less extreme ones.

questions.q: Give one statistical explanation of the Dunning-Kruger pattern.
questions.a: Self-estimates are loosely related to skill, so low performers must overestimate and high performers underestimate.

questions.q: What did Kruger and Dunning (1999) find about the bottom quartile?
questions.a: They rated themselves well above their actual rank.
